hints.title: Sorted Array Halving
hints.text: Scanning every element sequentially takes linear time. Given that the input array is already sorted, how can comparing against the middle element eliminate half the remaining candidates?

hints.title: Directional Elimination by Middle Comparison
hints.text: If the middle element is less than the target, the target must lie strictly to the right. If greater, it lies strictly to the left.

hints.title: Two Boundary Iterative Elimination
hints.text: Initialize left = 0 and right = len(nums) - 1. While left <= right, compute mid using left + (right - left) // 2. If nums[mid] equals target, return mid. If nums[mid] < target, advance left = mid + 1; otherwise set right = mid - 1. Return -1 if not found.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Halves the search range in each iteration using O(1) auxiliary variables.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Linear scan takes O(N) time. While it passes small inputs, it does not leverage the sorted invariant and is suboptimal for search queries.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Logarithmic O(log N) time with O(1) auxiliary space by repeatedly halving the search space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Safe midpoint calculation left + (right - left) // 2 to prevent integer overflow in languages with fixed-width integers, exact loop boundary left <= right, and correct pointer updates mid + 1 and mid - 1.

solutions.approach: Standard C++ Binary Search with Overflow Prevention
